key_note: Q (Dark Binding) is a long skillshot root and her main threat; it stops on the first unit hit, so standing behind minions limits her picks. E (Black Shield) blocks CC on an ally, so baiting it out before using your CC helps.
ult_note: R (Soul Shackles) chains nearby enemy champions, slowing and damaging them, then stuns anyone who has not broken the chain after a delay. She has to be close, so she often walks or flashes in; moving away from her fast breaks the chains.
spike_note: Level 6 adds a teamfight stun; her root is a threat all game, and she gets stronger with items that let her walk into fights safely.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 1 not 2 (Q is a catch from range, not a go-in tool); escape 0 since E blocks CC but gives no movement

key_note: Q (Darkin Daggers) is her poke and sends her packmates onto whoever it hits, so dodging it keeps the pack off you. E (Eviscerate) is her dash; trading or ganking after she uses it is safer.
ult_note: R (Hounds' Pursuit) sends her and her pack dashing onto a champion; after a takedown she reveals nearby enemies and can cast it again for a shield. Squishy carries caught alone are the target; grouping and holding CC for her limit the chain.
spike_note: Level 6 turns any isolated target into a kill threat. She is strongest with her first couple of damage items and falls off if the game drags on.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; roam 1 or 2, chose 2 for the speed from W (The Call of the Pack)

key_note: Q (Aqua Prison) is her only hard CC: a slow-landing bubble that stuns. Move sideways to dodge it; once it's on cooldown she has little to stop an all-in.
ult_note: R (Tidal Wave) is a wide wave that knocks up, slows and damages every enemy it crosses while speeding up allies. It can start a fight from range or stop a dive; avoid grouping in narrow paths when it's up.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6, when R adds a long-range engage or disengage. Her healing and empowered attacks grow as her items come in.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 0 not 1 (passive speed is mainly for allies)

key_note: Q (Siphoning Strike) grows each time he kills with it, so he wants to farm in peace. Harassing him while he farms, and jungle pressure before level 6, slow him down. W (Wither) is a strong slow, not a stun.
ult_note: R (Fury of the Sands) makes him bigger and tankier, adds attack range, lowers his Q cooldown and damages enemies around him. He can dive or win long fights while it's up. Kiting away until it ends is an option.
spike_note: Weak early; level 6 makes him hard to kill in lane, and he becomes a late-game threat once his Q has many stacks and he has a couple of items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 0 vs 1 was close, kept 1 because W lets him stick to a target

key_note: Q (hook) is his main engage. If it misses he's exposed for its cooldown. R is a point-and-click knock-up.
ult_note: Depth Charge chases one target and knocks up everyone along its path, then knocks up and stuns the target. It starts fights or picks off a carry from range; options are to spread out so it hits fewer people, and expect it on your most important carry.
spike_note: Threatening from level 2 with Dredge Line and his passive root, and again at level 6 with Depth Charge; he relies on his team's damage rather than his own.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: E (Tangle-Barbs) roots everything it passes through, and roots longer after passing a champion; it sets up Q (Blooming Burst). Dodging E removes most of her kill pressure, and she has no dash.
ult_note: R (Pop Blossom) knocks up enemies around her, then stuns them when she lands, and the windup is hidden while she's disguised. She can walk into a team looking like an ally or another unit; spreading out and watching for odd allies limit it.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when Pop Blossom gives her an area stun from a disguise; much stronger once her first damage item is done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Q (Javelin Toss) does more damage the farther it flies, and a hit starts a Hunt that makes her cougar Takedown and Pounce stronger. Keeping minions between you and her blocks the spear and her follow-up.
ult_note: R (Aspect Of The Cougar) swaps her between human form (spear, traps, heal) and cougar form (execute bite, pounce, swipe); she has it from the start, so level 6 changes less for her. Her threat is a spear hit followed by a cougar dive, so dodging spears limits her.
spike_note: Strongest early, especially from level 3 with all her abilities; she needs to snowball and loses impact the longer the game goes.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 not 3: strong invader but no hard CC for ganks; escape 2 not 3: one dash, Pounce, on a short cooldown; style could be farmer

key_note: W (Jubilant Veil) makes her and allies she touches dodge all basic attacks for a while, so attack trades into it are wasted; spells or backing off until it ends are options. She gains extra experience from last hits.
ult_note: R (Apotheosis) damages enemies around her and then pulls them toward her, dragging squishy carries into her and her team. It is short range, so keeping distance when she dashes in with E (Slipstream) limits it; allied heals and shields she boosts make her hard to kill.
spike_note: Strong level 2 all-ins with Q and E, a big jump at level 6, and dangerous once a couple of damage items are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; scaling 2 not 3; engage 2 because E is a direct dash to a target

key_note: E (Unspeakable Horror) fears you if you're still in range when the tether ends, so walking or dashing out breaks it. W (Shroud of Darkness) blocks one ability; baiting it out before using key CC works better.
ult_note: R (Paranoia) shrinks every enemy's sight and cuts their shared vision, then lets him launch at a champion from long range. After level 6 he can join fights in nearby lanes from fog; when the darkness starts, grouping and holding CC for his landing helps.
spike_note: Level 6 is his big jump: long-range ganks that start from fog. His first damage item makes him a strong pick-off threat for the rest of the game.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 1 because the fear can be walked out of; frontline 0 or 1, chose 1 for his passive healing and spell shield

key_note: W (Biggest Snowball Ever!) is his gank: it grows and speeds up the longer he rolls, then knocks up. Watch river and side paths for it; dodging the snowball usually ends the gank.
ult_note: R (Absolute Zero) creates a blizzard that slows enemies in a big area and deals massive damage at the end. Walk out of the zone rather than fighting in it; it's most dangerous around objectives and chokepoints.
spike_note: Ganks hard from level 3 with snowball and root; level 6 adds a big area threat for objectives. Most dangerous early, later a tanky utility jungler.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 2 not 3 (one engage tool); scaling 1 not 2 (early/mid peak)

key_note: Q (Undertow) slows and lowers armor, and picking the axe back up resets it; standing between him and where it lands makes pickups harder. He gains attack speed and life steal as his health drops, so long trades favor him.
ult_note: R (Ragnarok) makes him immune to disables while he keeps attacking, and passively gives armor and magic resist. He can run at carries through CC. Kiting so he can't attack, or saving CC for when it ends, are options.
spike_note: Strong early and again at level 6 when he can ignore CC; he peaks with his first couple of items and falls off in long games.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 vs 3 was close, picked lower

key_note: Command: Attack (Q) moves her Ball, and all her damage happens around it; stay away from where the Ball sits to dodge her poke and slows. She has no dash, so trading after she spends Q, or ganking her, works well.
ult_note: Command: Shockwave pulls everyone near her Ball toward it after a short delay, and the Ball can ride on an ally who dives in, turning their engage into a group pull. Options are to spread out and watch which ally carries the Ball.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 with Command: Shockwave; she scales steadily and is at her best in grouped team fights later in the game.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. scaling 2 or 3, picked lower. airborne from R launching enemies

key_note: E (Searing Charge) knocks up only if he hits terrain, often the pillar from Q (Volcanic Rupture). Staying away from walls and his Q pillar, or trading while E is down, avoids his main combo.
ult_note: R (Call of the Forge God) sends a massive elemental toward him that slows; if he recasts and charges into it, it knocks up everyone in its new path. It's a long teamfight engage; spreading out and stepping out of the line keep it to fewer targets.
spike_note: Strong at level 6 when his ult gives him a teamfight engage; scales well later because he can upgrade items for himself and his allies.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 because E is a dash but mostly used to engage

key_note: W (Shield Vault) dashes to a target and stuns, then Q (Comet Spear) and an empowered spell from his passive follow. E (Aegis Assault) blocks damage only from the front, so hitting him from behind or waiting it out works.
ult_note: R (Grand Starfall) launches him into the air to land as a comet at a chosen spot far away, so he can join fights in other lanes or flank. There's a wind-up before he lands; seeing it is a cue to leave the target area or punish his lane while he's gone.
spike_note: Strongest in the early levels, with all-in power from level 2; level 6 adds long-range roams. He falls off later if he doesn't get ahead early.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 3 because W stun is point-and-click

key_note: E (Heroic Charge) dashes to a target and pushes it back, stunning if it hits a wall, so fighting away from walls removes the stun. W (Steadfast Presence) stops dashes near her and grounds the dasher, so dashing near her is risky.
ult_note: R (Keeper's Verdict) is a channeled hammer strike that knocks enemies very far away, often sending a diver or key fighter out of the fight, or a contester away from an objective. Watching for the channel and stepping out of its path, or baiting it first, are options.
spike_note: Level 6 adds a fight-splitting knock-away; she gets very hard to kill once a couple of tank items are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; wiki says last changed 16.19 (this patch), check the kit; frontline 2 not 3

key_note: Q (Bone Skewer) pulls you in and E (Phantom Undertow) stuns along the phantom's path, so his all-in usually needs both. Out of sight he heals recent damage, so trades that let him walk into fog are worth less.
ult_note: R (Death From Below) blinks to and executes low-health enemies, can be recast after each kill, and gives gold to an ally who assisted. Low-health champions near him are at risk; backing off rather than fighting on low health is the main counter.
spike_note: Level 2 gives him the hook-and-stun all-in, and level 6 adds a resetting execute. He is strongest early and in skirmishes, and tends to fall off as games go long.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 or 3, chose 2 for his low durability; engage 2 or 3, chose 2

key_note: W (Terrashape) is a dash that takes an element from nearby terrain, and E (Audacity) dashes to you. She wants short burst trades; trade back or gank when both dashes are on cooldown.
ult_note: R (Supreme Display of Talent) sends a shockwave that detonates the terrain it hits, stunning and damaging enemies nearby. It's deadliest when you're grouped near walls, river or brush; spread out and stay in open ground when she's near.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6, when R gives her a team-fight stun. Very dangerous once her first damage item is done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 1 (Q effect depends on element, text gives no detail); escape 2 not 3 (two dashes, both used to go in)

key_note: E (Vault) dashes to a target, interrupts them and leaps back to range, so it is both her trade and her escape; trading or ganking right after she uses it is an option. Q (Blinding Assault) also hinders sight.
ult_note: R (Behind Enemy Lines) lets her fly around at great speed on a very short cooldown, so after level 6 she can roam to other lanes and back quickly; ending it damages nearby enemies. Warning other lanes when she is missing is an option.
spike_note: Annoying from range early; level 6 turns her into a fast roamer, and her first damage item lets her burst squishy targets.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 vs 3 was close, picked lower (stronger into melee tops)

key_note: Grand Entrance (W) is his knock-up engage, often extended by flying to an ally with Battle Dance (E) first; when W is on cooldown he can't start a fight, so that's the window to trade.
ult_note: The Quickness gives him Move Speed and charms every enemy he touches, so he can run through a whole team. With Grand Entrance it starts fights from far away; options are to spread out and keep a dash or disengage ready when he has it.
spike_note: Threatening from level 2 with Grand Entrance and Battle Dance together, and much more at level 6 with The Quickness.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. scaling 1 or 2, picked lower

key_note: Q (Powerball) gives him big speed for ganks and E (Frenzying Taunt) forces you to attack him. Vision on his paths gives time to walk away before Q reaches you; attacking into W (Defensive Ball Curl) returns damage to you.
ult_note: R (Soaring Slam) slams an area to damage and slow, and knocks up enemies near the center if cast during Powerball. It lets him start fights from farther away and adds to tower dives; spreading out reduces it.
spike_note: Strong ganker once he has Q and E; level 6 adds the slam, and he gets harder to kill and hits harder as armor and magic resist items come in.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: W (Burrow) lets her travel fast underground and knock up nearby enemies on Un-burrow; E (Tunnel) leaves re-usable tunnels for surprise ganks. Destroying tunnel entrances by standing on them cuts her routes.
ult_note: R (Void Rush) makes her briefly untargetable and lunges at a champion she has damaged recently, for heavy damage based on max Health. It finishes targets trying to flee a fight; staying out of her reach after she has hit you limits it.
spike_note: Strong ganks from level 3 once she can burrow and knock up; level 6 adds a finishing lunge. She is best early and mid game and weakens as enemies get tankier.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 not 3: strong ganker, could be 3

key_note: W (Ferromancy: Crash Down) is her engage: she dismounts, knocking up nearby enemies, and is then slowed while dismounted. Punishing her right after W, or keeping distance while E (Full Tilt) speeds her toward you, are options.
ult_note: R (Magnet Storm) pulls nearby enemies toward her and keeps dragging them for a short while, holding a group in place for her team. It is short range, so she usually needs E or W to reach a group first; spreading out and watching her approach limits how many she catches.
spike_note: Threatening all-ins from level 2; level 6 makes her teamfight engage much bigger, and she is strongest in mid-game fights.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Q (Handshake) roots the first enemy hit and can then throw them, often into her team. Standing behind minions blocks it, and trading or engaging while it's on cooldown is much safer.
ult_note: R (Hostile Takeover) sends a wave that makes enemies hit go Berserk and attack their own side. It punishes grouped teams in choke points and stops dives; spreading out limits it. W (Bailout) can also keep a dying ally alive if they get a takedown.
spike_note: Level 6 gives her one of the strongest team fight ultimates. She is most dangerous in grouped fights from mid game on.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; no airborne tag, unsure whether the Q throw counts as a knock-back

key_note: Fury is his power: above 50 Fury his Q heals more and W (Ruthless Predator) stuns for 1.5 seconds and breaks shields. Trade when his Fury is low and avoid long fights when it's full.
ult_note: R (Dominus) gives him bonus Health, damages enemies around him and builds Fury over time. It makes his all-ins and dives much harder to beat; back off when he turns it on rather than trading into it.
spike_note: Strong from level 3 with his full combo and again at level 6; he peaks early and mid game, so falling behind him early is hard to recover from.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 2 not 3 (W is point-and-click but short unless empowered); Q named by key only (its name contains an item name)

key_note: In brush his basic attack leaps to the target, so staying away from brush near him blunts his burst. At max Ferocity his E (Bola Strike) roots, so dodging the bola is the main option.
ult_note: R (Thrill of the Hunt) camouflages him, gives move speed and reveals the nearest enemy champion around him; he can then leap without brush. It threatens isolated carries. Staying near teammates and away from brush while it's up are options.
spike_note: Level 6 lets him jump on isolated champions from far away; with his first damage item and a few kills for his trophies he can burst squishy targets quickly.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 vs 3 was close, picked lower

key_note: Valor (E) and the three Broken Wings (Q) dashes are her trades and her escape; once they're used she can't get away or chase. Trading back while Q and E are on cooldown works well, and Ki Burst (W) stuns up close.
ult_note: Blade of the Exile gives her more attack damage and range, and lets her fire Wind Slash, a powerful ranged attack, once. It makes her all-ins much stronger; options are to respect her kill range when you're low, and fight after Wind Slash is used.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when Blade of the Exile makes her all-ins much stronger; strong with her first damage item and dangerous in a side lane after a couple.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. early 2 or 3, picked lower

key_note: Q (Flamespitter) is most of his damage and hits harder in Danger Zone, so he wants to stay close. Trading when he Overheats and can't cast, or staying out of Q range, takes away his trades.
ult_note: R (The Equalizer) lays a wall of fire that damages and slows anyone standing in it, splitting teamfights and zoning around objectives. Not grouping in narrow spaces and leaving the fire quickly limit the damage.
spike_note: Strong early, and a big jump at level 6 when The Equalizer swings teamfights and skirmishes; dangerous once his first damage item is done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 with lane_bully, could be 3

key_note: W (Rune Prison) roots anyone already hit by E (Spell Flux) and only slows otherwise. Q (Overload) is his main damage and resets often. Trading when W is down, and away from Flux-marked minions, limits him.
ult_note: R (Realm Warp) opens a portal to a nearby spot and, after a few seconds, teleports allies standing near it, so his team can flank, rotate to an objective or escape together. Watching the portal and its exit gives time to react.
spike_note: Weak in early fights; level 6 adds group teleports, and he gets much stronger as items raise his mana and ability power, with a strong mid to late game.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 2 not 3: point-and-click root needs E first; Realm Warp range is local, so no ult_join tag

key_note: W blocks projectiles, so bait it before throwing skillshots. Her R needs her style meter maxed first.
ult_note: R (Inferno Trigger) shoots every enemy around her repeatedly once her style combo is built, and she chains it with E (Wild Rush), which resets on champion kills. Hard CC on her, or not grouping tightly around her when her meter is full, limits it.
spike_note: Strong level 2 all-ins, a big jump at level 6 when R comes online, and very dangerous once a couple of damage items let her reset through fights.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: Q (Arctic Assault) is her engage, a charge that knocks you up. W (Winter's Wrath) builds Frost stacks and E (Permafrost) stuns at max stacks, so leaving before stacks build keeps you safe.
ult_note: R (Glacial Prison) is a thrown bola that stuns the first champion hit and slows everyone nearby; it's her main team fight engage and a pick tool for ganks. Spreading out and not walking in a line with teammates limit how many it catches.
spike_note: Level 6 makes her ganks very reliable. She gets tankier with each defensive item and stays an engage threat all game, but her damage stays modest.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; scaling 1 or 2, chose 1; escape 1 since Q is mostly used to engage

key_note: W (Last Embrace) is her only hard CC: a wave that roots you and everyone near you after a delay. Her attacks are slow and long-ranged, so she is weak to all-ins once W misses.
ult_note: R (Dawning Shadow) is a global beam that shields her allies and damages enemies in its center. It can save an ally losing a fight in another lane or finish someone low anywhere; expect it when chasing a kill.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 with her global R. Her Mist keeps raising her damage and range, so she gets stronger the longer the game goes.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 not 2 (E camouflage and speed, no dash)

key_note: Q (High Note) is her poke, and her passive makes every third basic spell cast twice; counting her casts and avoiding trades when the double cast is ready are options. E (Beat Drop) impairs movement in a line.
ult_note: R (Encore) charms every champion it hits, and its range grows with each champion it passes, ally or enemy, so it can catch a whole team from far away. Spreading out, and not lining up with teammates, limits it.
spike_note: Level 6 adds a fight-winning R; her damage, heals and shields grow steadily with items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 1 vs 2 was close, picked lower (support row; bot Seraphine pokes harder)

key_note: Haymaker (W) grows with the damage he's taken and deals true damage in its center; avoid the middle of it. Facebreaker (E) only stuns with enemies on both sides of him, so don't stand opposite your minions.
ult_note: The Show Stopper carries one champion and slams them down, damaging and slowing everyone near the landing spot. He can grab a frontliner and throw them into your carries; options are to keep carries spread away from the frontline.
spike_note: Strong in lane early and again at level 6 with The Show Stopper; best in the mid game, in fights where he can take damage and return it with Haymaker.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. early 2 or 3, picked lower. escape 0: Q speed only works toward champions. scaling 1 or 2, picked lower

key_note: Q (Deceive) turns him invisible and teleports him, often behind you for a big hit, and W (Jack In The Box) boxes fear when triggered. Vision on his paths and not fighting near his boxes limit him; after Q he has far less escape.
ult_note: R (Hallucinate) makes a clone that attacks and explodes into three mini boxes when it dies. It hides which Shaco is real and covers his escape; focusing the real one and not killing the clone next to your team avoid the fears.
spike_note: Strongest early, with ganks and invades from level 3; spikes again at level 6 with the clone, then falls off if he isn't ahead.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Q (Twilight Assault) hits much harder when it collides with a champion on its way back; staying out of the line between him and his blade avoids it. E (Shadow Dash) taunt is his engage, so trade after it's down.
ult_note: R (Stand United) shields an allied champion anywhere on the map and teleports him to them shortly after. From level 6, check where he is before diving any lane; the delay gives time to finish the kill or leave, and pushing his lane while he's gone punishes it.
spike_note: Solid early trades with Q, and level 6 is his big jump because of the map-wide ult; he stays useful late as a tank and protector rather than a damage threat.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; frontline 2 not 3: tank kit but often builds some damage

key_note: Before level 6 her only crowd control is the slow on E (Molten Burst), so her early ganks are weak; invading or contesting objectives while she farms are options. W (Inferno Aegis) shields and speeds her up.
ult_note: R (Dragon's Descent) turns her into a dragon and leaps her forward, making enemies along the path flee, and empowers her basic abilities while in dragon form. It is her engage into fights and objectives, so keeping the team out of one leap line helps.
spike_note: Weak early; level 6 unlocks dragon form for engages and fights, and she gets much stronger once a couple of items are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; kit looks reworked, partly new to me: scores lean on the ability text; unsure what limits dragon form

key_note: E (Fling) throws you behind him, and landing in his W (Mega Adhesive) roots you too. Chasing him through Q (Poison Trail) is usually a losing trade; letting him go and taking the wave or tower is often better.
ult_note: R (Insanity Potion) gives him a burst of combat stats and makes his poison trail cut healing, so he can run through a team and fling a target out of position. Spacing out and not chasing him while it lasts help.
spike_note: Level 6 makes him much harder to kill and better at diving into teams. With a couple of items he is a strong split-pusher who is hard to catch.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 or 2, chose 1 (speed and grounding, no dash)

key_note: Q (Decimating Smash) only knocks up and stuns if he charges it long enough, and the charge shows in front of him. Step out of it; he has no dash, so a dodged Q leaves him open.
ult_note: R (Unstoppable Onslaught) is a long charge he can steer that knocks up the first enemy hit, harder the farther he charged. He can use it to roam or start a fight from far off; it's easy to sidestep when you see it coming.
spike_note: Level 6 adds a long-range engage. He gains max Health from kills all game, so he becomes a very hard tank late.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: E (Spell Shield) blocks one enemy ability and gives her health and speed; baiting it with a less important spell before using key CC is an option. W (Ricochet) and Q (Boomerang Blade) let her push waves fast.
ult_note: R (On The Hunt) gives her whole team a burst of move speed to engage, chase or run, and her attacks lower her spell cooldowns. Watching for a fast team rush and holding disengage tools for it are options.
spike_note: Weaker in early trades but shoves waves fast; she scales with crit items and is strongest once a couple of them are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; waveclear 3 because pushing is her lane identity

key_note: Ixtal's Impact (E) charges through terrain and stuns you if he slams you into a wall; stay away from walls when he can reach you, and expect ganks from over walls rather than along the paths.
ult_note: Impale suppresses enemy champions in front of him and drags them wherever he walks, often back into his team or under his tower. It's a strong pick and engage tool; options are to stay out of his front and keep peel ready for carries.
spike_note: Strong gank threat from early levels with Ixtal's Impact and a big jump at level 6 with Impale; as a tank he stays useful all game once he has defensive items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. scaling 1 or 2, picked lower. escape 2 from E through terrain

key_note: Q (Super Scorcher Breath) builds Dragon Practice stacks that make his abilities stronger all game. Pressuring him early before stacks build, and when E (Flap, Flap, Flap) is on cooldown, gives the best windows.
ult_note: R (MMOOOMMMM!) has his mom breathe fire from above, dealing extra damage and slowing enemies in the center of the fire. It finishes low targets and covers fights; dodging the center avoids the slow.
spike_note: Weak early; grows steadily as Dragon Practice stacks build, gets better at level 6, and becomes a late-game threat with a couple of items and many stacks.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Q (Hymn of Valor) hits the two nearest enemies and is her poke, but she is very fragile and has no dash. Going in when her W (Aria of Perseverance) heal and shield are down wins most fights.
ult_note: R (Crescendo) stuns every enemy champion it hits and damages them, so it can start or flip a team fight from range. Not standing in a line with teammates limits how many it catches; once it's used she has little to protect herself.
spike_note: Weak in the first levels; level 6 adds a team-wide stun, and she gets stronger with each item, healing and speeding up her team in long fights.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; scaling 2 not 3: scales well but isn't a carry

key_note: Q (Starcall) is her poke and heals her when it hits a champion, so dodging it cuts her sustain. W (Astral Infusion) costs her own health, so pressuring her directly beats her healing.
ult_note: R (Wish) instantly heals her and every allied champion wherever they are on the map, which can save a losing fight or dive in another lane. Finishing fast, or waiting until she has used R, keeps it from undoing a kill.
spike_note: Strong sustain from the first levels; level 6 adds map-wide healing, and her heals keep growing with items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 1 because the E root only lands if they stay in the zone

key_note: E (Nevermove) goes out and roots on the way back, then he can pull rooted champions in. Watching the return path and dodging it beats most of his kill pressure.
ult_note: R (Demonic Ascension) drains health from everyone near him and lasts as long as he keeps draining champions, so long close-range fights feed him. Bursting him early, or kiting back until it ends, works better; Demonflare adds a slow.
spike_note: Level 6 makes him a durable team fight drain tank. He gets stronger with each item and is hard to kill in drawn-out fights.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 1 or 2, chose 2 for the E root and pull

key_note: W (Kingslayer) lunges at you and heals him, so short trades favor him. E (Abscond / Abduct) is both his engage and his escape; trade or gank once it's on cooldown.
ult_note: R (Hijack) steals an enemy ultimate and he can cast it freely, so his threat depends on your team's ults. Expect your own strongest engage or damage ult used against you and play around whose ult he took.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6, when he can steal an ult. Strong again once his first item is done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 1 for the short knock-up on E recast (not in Riot text, from memory)

key_note: E (Scatter the Weak) knocks enemies back and stuns anyone hit by a Dark Sphere; staying out of line with her spheres saves a lot of damage. She has no dash, so ganks work well once E is down.
ult_note: R (Unleashed Power) throws all her Dark Spheres at one champion, so it hits harder the more spheres are out, and her passive upgrade lets it execute low targets. Fighting when few spheres are up, or after she uses R, are options.
spike_note: Level 6 lets her burst a squishy target with R; her passive upgrades her spells as she levels and deals damage, so she keeps growing.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Each of his hits builds An Acquired Taste; at three stacks Tongue Lash (Q) stuns and he can Devour you. Short trades that don't let stacks build, and staying out of Q range, stop him setting up a kill.
ult_note: Devour swallows a champion for a few seconds: an enemy takes magic damage and is taken out of the fight, while an ally is shielded. He uses it to save carries or remove one enemy; options are to avoid three stacks and expect him to save whoever you dive.
spike_note: Solid in lane from early levels; level 6 lets him swallow allies to save them, and he gets more dangerous as his health grows, since his attacks scale with it.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. escape 1: W dive repositions but is slow. point_click_cc from R on enemies

key_note: Q (Threaded Volley) is her main damage; W (Seismic Shove) throws you, and being thrown or dashing through E (Unraveled Earth) mines stuns you. Not dashing over her minefield and dodging W keep her combo from landing.
ult_note: R (Weaver's Wall) makes a very long wall that she rides, letting her reach other lanes fast, or cut off a team's escape or engage. After level 6, checking where she is before fighting helps; the wall can also split your team.
spike_note: Strong from level 6 when the wall lets her roam to other lanes and split fights; dangerous once her first damage item is done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 because R surfing is slow to set up

key_note: Q (Noxian Diplomacy) leaps to a target and crits up close; W (Rake) is his poke and slow. E (Assassin's Path) vaults any wall, so he reaches other lanes fast; warding his routes and calling it when he leaves lane limits him.
ult_note: R (Shadow Assault) throws out a ring of blades and makes him invisible with extra speed; the blades converge where he reappears. It lets him burst a squishy target and slip away; grouping up and vision on his likely angle make it harder.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when he can burst a squishy target and vanish; with his first damage item he hunts roams and isolated targets, and he falls off if he can't snowball.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 not 3: strong but less than the anchors

key_note: E (Dazzle) stuns after a short delay and can be cast from the ally holding W (Bastion), so it can come from an odd angle. Walking out of the beam during the delay avoids it.
ult_note: R (Cosmic Radiance) makes nearby allies invulnerable for a short duration after a delay, which can turn a dive or teamfight his way. Backing off until it ends, rather than spending big damage into it, is usually the best response.
spike_note: Main jump at level 6 when R can make his team invulnerable; he gets more useful as items add tankiness and healing.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 1 not 2 (level 2-3 all-ins depend on his lane partner)

key_note: Q blind cancels your autos for a few seconds, so trade right after he uses it. After 6, don't walk through unwarded bushes (mushrooms).
ult_note: R (Noxious Trap) places hidden mushrooms that slow and poison anyone who steps on them, and they bounce off each other for range. Over time they cover the jungle and side lanes, so clearing them or walking warded paths beats face-checking brush.
spike_note: Level 6 starts his mushroom field. He grows with magic damage items, and his traps add up over the game to control the map.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: Q (hook) is his engage; a miss is your window. Lantern can pull in a second engager.
ult_note: R (The Box) surrounds him with walls that slow and damage anyone who breaks through. It cuts off escapes and splits fights; avoid fighting inside it and only walk through a wall when you have to.
spike_note: Strong from level 2 with hook and lantern; he gains Armor and Ability Power from souls over the whole game.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: W (Rocket Jump) is her engage and her only escape; trading or ganking after she uses it is an option. E (Explosive Charge) puts a bomb on a target that explodes after a short delay, so stepping away from allies limits the blast.
ult_note: R (Buster Shot) knocks one target back hard and widens the E bomb blast. She uses it to peel a diver off herself or to knock someone into her team. Diving her once it's used, or not fighting with your back to her team, are options.
spike_note: Threatening all-in from level 2 with E and W, again at level 6; her passive adds range as she levels, so she gets safer and stronger as the game goes on.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 1 vs 2 was close, picked lower since W is risky for her

key_note: Chomp (Q) steals attack damage with each bite and has a very short cooldown, so long trades favor him; short trades work better. Pillar of Ice (E) can cut off your escape path.
ult_note: Subjugate steals part of one target's health, armor and magic resistance, and doubles the steal over the next 4 seconds. It shreds tanks and wins duels; options are to avoid long one-on-one fights after level 6 and to kite him rather than stand still.
spike_note: Strong early duelist with a jump at level 6 when Subjugate lets him beat tanks and bruisers; at his best in long fights and pushing side lanes.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. invade_strong and jungle style uncertain

key_note: Q (Bloodlust) spends Fury to heal him, and his damage rises as he gets lower. Short trades when his Fury is empty or Q was just used are safest; W (Mocking Shout) slows only if your back is turned to him.
ult_note: R (Undying Rage) stops him from dying for a short time, so he dives towers and backlines and outlasts burst. Kiting or crowd control until it ends, then focusing him, is the usual answer; it also makes him a strong split pusher.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when Undying Rage lets him all-in safely; much stronger once his first crit item is done, and he scales well late.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 1 because E is a dash but he has no hard CC

key_note: W (Pick a Card) picks a card for his next attack, and the gold card stuns. Staying out of his attack range while he's choosing avoids it; he has no dash, so ganks work well after he uses W.
ult_note: R (Destiny) reveals every enemy champion on the map, then lets him Gate to any spot after 1.5 seconds. From level 6 he can arrive in any lane with a stun for a gank; when his ult goes up, side lanes are safest backing off.
spike_note: Weak in early fights; level 6 is his big jump since he can gank any lane, and he gets stronger with each item while always threatening to join a fight.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; gold card stun isn't spelled out in the ability text; cc 2 not 3: point-and-click but needs the right card and an attack

key_note: Q (Ambush) camouflages him and speeds him up, so he can appear from fog for a surprise all-in or slip away. Vision in brush and on his paths, and punishing him while Q is on cooldown, are the main counters.
ult_note: R (Spray and Pray) lets him shoot over a great distance with bolts that pierce every enemy in a line, so he can shred a group from behind his frontline, often right after leaving camouflage. Not lining up with teammates and reaching him with dive or long-range CC are the main answers.
spike_note: Fairly weak early apart from surprise ganks; level 6 adds a strong teamfight ult, and he becomes a major threat once a couple of damage items are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: E (Blazing Stampede) gives him speed and stuns on his first attack against each target, which is how he starts fights. Its recast makes him immune to immobilizing effects for a moment, so saving CC until that ends works better.
ult_note: R (Wingborne Storm) is a basic ability, not a true ultimate: a storm around him that damages and slows, with a stronger recast. He has no map-wide ultimate, so the threat is his sustained fighting rather than one big cooldown.
spike_note: No single level spike, since his four abilities rank up evenly. His first item is a big jump for ganks and duels.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; scaling 1 or 2, chose 1; spikes left blank (no ultimate level); style ganker vs farmer unsure

key_note: E (Disdain) is his engage: a charge that shields him and hurls the first champion it catches. Minions don't stop it, so keep your distance and side-step; once E is down he's slow and easy to kite.
ult_note: R (Fear Beyond Death) impales the first champion hit; below a health threshold he can execute them. Champions in front can block it, so stay healthy or out of its line when it's up.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 with his execute. As W ranks up its cooldown drops until it can stay on, which makes him a strong sustained fighter.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; airborne left off (unsure the E flip counts as a knock-back)

key_note: Q (Piercing Arrow) is long-range poke that grows the longer he charges it. W (Blighted Quiver) stacks from his attacks pop with his other spells, so trading after he stacks you favors him. He has no dash, so ganks work well.
ult_note: R (Chain of Corruption) immobilizes the first champion hit and spreads to nearby champions, so it can catch a whole group or start a fight. Spreading out when it's up is an option; it's his only way to lock someone down.
spike_note: Strong poke from early on; level 6 adds a pick and teamfight R, and he gets stronger with a couple of damage items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Condemn (E) knocks you back and stuns you if you hit a wall, so fight her away from walls. She's weak early and has short range for a marksman, so trading or ganking before she has items is the time to punish her.
ult_note: Final Hour gives her more attack damage, a faster Tumble and invisibility during Tumble, so she's hard to target in fights. Options are to fight while it's down, or burst her before she can Tumble, and keep ways to reveal her for fights.
spike_note: Weak early; level 6 adds Final Hour, and she becomes very dangerous after a couple of items, when Silver Bolts' true damage hurts even tanks.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. top Vayne plays more like a lane bully; a top role row may be worth adding

key_note: E (Event Horizon) is a cage that stuns enemies who pass through it, and his only defense; he has no dash. Baiting the cage, or fighting while it's down, leaves him open.
ult_note: R (Primordial Burst) blasts one champion for big magic damage that grows with their missing health, so it executes low targets. Staying out of his range when hurt, and committing after he's used it, reduce the risk.
spike_note: Weak early, but Phenomenal Evil Power grows his ability power forever; big jump at level 6 for the execute and very strong late with a couple of items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: Q (Plasma Fission) splits and slows, setting up E (Tectonic Disruption) knock-up and W (Void Rift) poke; 3 hits trigger bonus true damage from his passive. He has no dash, so dodging Q and E and walking up when they're down works.
ult_note: R (Life Form Disintegration Ray) is a channelled beam that follows his cursor for 2.5 seconds and deals true damage to champions his passive has marked. Crowd control on him ends it early; stepping out of the beam's line works since he must turn it.
spike_note: Strong poke from the early levels and a big jump at level 6; he gets more dangerous with each item and his damage is hard to avoid when he's ahead.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 1: E knock-up can start a fight but he is immobile

key_note: Her passive (Doom 'n Gloom) periodically makes her next ability fear, and dashing near her marks you and interrupts the dash. Baiting the empowered fear out first, then trading or dashing in, is an option.
ult_note: R (Shadow Surge) fires a long-range missile that marks an enemy champion; recasting dashes her to them for damage. It lets her finish low targets or jump onto a carry from far away, so after level 6 low-health targets near her are at risk.
spike_note: Level 6 gives her a long-range dash-in burst, the main jump; her first damage item makes her combo lethal on squishy targets.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 0 since R dashes toward enemies; peel for the anti-dash fear

key_note: Q (Vault Breaker) is a charged dash that knocks back, her main gank tool. The charge-up is visible, so moving away early or saving a dash until she commits helps; trading after it's used is safe.
ult_note: R (Cease and Desist) locks onto a chosen champion, knocking aside anyone in the way, and knocks the target up on arrival. Backline carries are the usual target; peel and CC saved for her landing work better than body-blocking.
spike_note: Level 6 makes ganks on one target close to guaranteed. She is strongest early to mid game with her first damage items, then becomes more of a lock-down tool.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 or 2, chose 1 (Q is mostly used to engage); scaling 1 or 2, chose 1

key_note: W (Spectral Maw) is his only CC: a charged dash that stuns the first enemy hit. Stand behind minions to block it; without it he can't lock you down.
ult_note: R (Heartbreaker) teleports him a short way to execute a champion and knocks their allies away. Every kill lets him possess the dead enemy and get a free R, so deny him the first kill or focus him once he possesses someone.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6. With a few items, each kill in a fight snowballs into a possession and another R.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; style farmer is a guess (skirmisher who farms toward resets)

key_note: E (Hextech Ray) is his main poke and waveclear in a line; stepping out of its path limits his damage. Q (Siphon Power) shields him and empowers his next attack, so short trades often favor him when it's ready.
ult_note: R (Arcane Storm) is a storm he can move that damages everyone near it and interrupts channels; in teamfights it zones a whole area. Fighting away from it or spreading out are options. Once upgraded, it grows when champions die in it.
spike_note: Each upgrade from Hex Fragments makes him stronger and level 6 adds a big teamfight R; he gets much stronger after a couple of items and kills.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; scaling 2 vs 3 was close, picked lower; W stun is slow to land so cc 1

key_note: Transfusion (Q) is his damage and healing, and gets much stronger when his resource is full. Sanguine Pool (W) makes him untargetable for 2 seconds and is his only escape, so gank or all-in after he's used it.
ult_note: Hemoplague infects an area so enemies take more damage, then hits each of them after a few seconds and heals him per champion hit. It rewards him for grouped fights; options are to spread out and avoid clumping in its area.
spike_note: Weak early but a big jump at level 6 with Hemoplague; he scales hard with items, so punishing him in lane before then matters.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. escape 2: W is untargetable but on a long cooldown

key_note: Q (Thundering Smash) speeds him toward you and stuns on his next attack; it's his only hard CC and the start of every all-in. Keeping out of reach until it's used, then trading, limits him; W (Frenzied Maul) heals on a second hit.
ult_note: R (Stormbringer) leaps to a spot, slowing and damaging enemies there and giving him bonus health, and towers near the landing are disabled for a while. That makes tower dives strong after level 6; a tower is not a safe spot while it's up.
spike_note: Strong early with Q; big jump at level 6 when Stormbringer turns off towers for dives; best in the middle of the game and less dominant late.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2, could be 3

key_note: W (Blood Hunt) gives him big Move Speed toward anyone below 50% health, and his passive heals him when he is low. Avoid fighting him while low; long fights favor him, so short burst trades work better.
ult_note: R (Infinite Duress) is a leap that suppresses the first champion it hits for 1.5 seconds, and it reaches farther with his bonus Move Speed. From level 6 his ganks are deadly; keeping a tank between him and your carry makes it hit the wrong target.
spike_note: Strong ganks and duels early, with a big jump at level 6 when his leap locks down a target; he falls off as enemies build more damage and burst.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 not 3 and engage 1: Q lunge is his only gap closer before level 6

key_note: E (Bladecaller) calls back her dropped feathers and roots enemies they pass through, so staying off the line between her and her feathers avoids the root. Feathers come from Q (Double Daggers) and attacks after spells.
ult_note: R (Featherstorm) makes her leap untargetable and throw a fan of daggers that leaves feathers to recall, so she can dodge an engage and set up a multi-person root. Spending your engage or big ability after she has used R is the usual answer.
spike_note: Level 6 gives her an untargetable dodge and root setup; she gets much stronger once her first couple of damage items are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; cc 1 not 2 since the root depends on feather placement

key_note: His poke comes from long-range skillshots, Q (Arcanopulse) and W (Eye of Destruction), and E (Shocking Orb) is his stun. He has no dash, so closing in after E misses or ganking him works well.
ult_note: R (Rite of the Arcane) roots him in place for several very long-range barrages, so he can finish low-health targets from afar or help nearby lanes. He can't move while casting, so diving him or stepping out of range breaks it.
spike_note: Level 6 adds long-range finishing power. He gets stronger with each damage item, and his poke makes sieges and objective fights hard to start into him.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; waveclear 2 or 3, chose 2

key_note: E (Audacious Charge) is his gap-closer, with more range on targets marked by W, and the third hit of Q (Three Talon Strike) knocks you up. Ward his entrances and back off once his E lands.
ult_note: R (Crescent Guard) damages everyone nearby, knocks back all but his challenged target, and makes him impervious to damage from champions outside the circle. Fight him from inside the circle or wait it out.
spike_note: Strong from his first clear and ganks hard at level 3; level 6 makes his dives safer. Peaks early and mid game, then falls off.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; frontline 1 not 2 (diver, R helps him survive dives)

key_note: W (Wind Wall) blocks projectiles. His R only works on knocked-up targets.
ult_note: R (Last Breath) blinks to an airborne enemy and keeps every airborne enemy nearby in the air; it combos with any knock-up on his team. Avoiding his Q tornado and his allies' knock-ups leaves him without it.
spike_note: Gets strong once his crit items come together; after level 6 every knock-up on his team can turn into a big play.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: Mortal Steel (Q) dashes him forward and knocks you up on its second stack, so step away when he has it charged. Soul Unbound (E) always pulls him back to his body, so standing near his body lets you punish him.
ult_note: Fate Sealed blinks him behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him, starting a team fight on its own. Options are to avoid standing in a line with teammates and stay spread when he's looking for an engage.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 with Fate Sealed; his passive raises his critical strike chance, so he gets much stronger with each critical strike item.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. escape 2 or 3, picked lower. scaling 2 or 3, picked lower

key_note: W (Dark Procession) builds a wall that traps you while his Walkers and E (Mourning Mist) chase. Attacking the wall to break it, and fighting while W is on cooldown, make his all-ins much weaker.
ult_note: R (Eulogy of the Isles) summons the Maiden, who makes his attacks on her target hit harder and raises Walkers from dead enemies. It makes him a strong split pusher; sending someone who can duel him to his side lane, or forcing fights elsewhere, are the usual answers.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when the Maiden joins his pushing; much stronger once his first damage item is done, and he grows into a split push threat.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 1, could be 2

key_note: Q (Cultivation of Spirit) gives her Attack Speed and on-hit damage and spreads her attacks to nearby enemies, so standing near minions or allies spreads her damage. Before her ult she has no dash, only speed from E.
ult_note: R (Transcend One's Self) upgrades her basic abilities: W becomes a laser that damages and slows, and E becomes a dash. It gives her more reach and mobility in fights, so engaging before she uses it, or after it ends, is safer.
spike_note: Like most marksmen she wants items, with a jump at level 6 when her ult adds a dash; she becomes a main damage threat with a couple of items.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; new to me: scores from ability text only

key_note: W (You and Me!) attaches her to an ally and makes her untargetable to everything except turrets, so she can't be focused. Hitting her when she detaches, or punishing the ally she rides, is the main way to pressure her.
ult_note: R (Final Chapter) channels five waves that damage enemies and heal allies while she can stay attached, which swings longer fights her team's way. Short burst fights, or catching her while detached, limit it.
spike_note: Weak in early fights; level 6 adds a teamfight heal, and she grows stronger as her ally gets items, most of all with the ally she has bonded with most.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; text no longer mentions a root on R, so cc 0; roam 1 not 2

key_note: W (Dreaded Return) stabs in a line and pulls enemies hit toward him, setting up the knock-up recast of Q (The Darkin Glaive). Dodging the stab, or trading after it's used, takes away most of his all-in.
ult_note: R (Grim Deliverance) has him rise then stab down, damaging enemies and healing him for part of the damage. It extends his fights more than it affects the map; a full Determination bar also lets him revive, so finishing him may take two tries.
spike_note: Level 6 adds burst and healing to his all-in. His passive stacks attack damage as he fights champions, so long fights favor him.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; new to me: scores from ability text only

key_note: E (Elastic Slingshot) launches him in from a distance and is on a long cooldown early. Watch for him in fog near your lane and punish him when E is down. Killing his blobs denies his heals and revive.
ult_note: R (Let's Bounce!) has him bounce four times, knocking up and slowing enemies hit. It's a strong team-fight engage and disengage; spreading out limits how many he catches, and after he 'dies', kill his bloblets to stop the revive.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6, when R adds area knock-ups to his E engage. Gets steadily tankier with items and is a hard frontline late.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; engage 2 not 3 (E is strong but long cooldown early)

key_note: W shadow is his escape and his trade. Gank right after he uses it.
ult_note: R (Death Mark) makes him untargetable, dashes to one champion and marks them; after 3 seconds the mark repeats part of the damage he dealt. It threatens squishy carries. Staying near allies and saving defensive tools for when the mark pops are options.
spike_note: Level 6 lets him kill a squishy target in one combo; his first damage item makes him a threat to every squishy lane.
notes: roam, waveclear, frontline, ult_note, spike_note drafted by llm from 16.19.1

key_note: Spark Surge (E) is her only dash and lets her vault over terrain; it has a long cooldown early, so trade or gank right after she uses it. Burst Fire (Q) is treated as her attack, so it's her main lane damage.
ult_note: Lightning Crash damages enemies around her and overcharges her, giving damage and stacking Move Speed that grows each time she hits a champion, and chains Burst Fire between enemies. Options are to wait it out or catch her before it's up.
spike_note: Weak early; level 6 adds Lightning Crash, and she gets much stronger with attack speed items, becoming a dangerous late-game carry once a few are done.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text. scaling 2 or 3, picked lower

key_note: Q (Bouncing Bomb) is his main poke, and W (Satchel Charge) knocks enemies away and launches him to safety. Staying behind minions and engaging after W is used give the best window; he struggles when he can't keep distance.
ult_note: R (Mega Inferno Bomb) lands an enormous distance away, so he can finish low enemies in other lanes or open teamfights from far off. Spreading out and not lingering on low health in the open limit it.
spike_note: Big jump at level 6 when his ult can finish targets far away; strong at taking towers with W, and again once his first damage item is done.

key_note: Q (Time Bomb) sticks to the nearest unit and explodes after 3 seconds, and a second bomb on the same target stuns. Moving away from allies when a bomb lands on you limits the blast, and trading once both bombs are down is safest.
ult_note: R (Chronoshift) puts a rune on one ally that sends them back in time if they take lethal damage, undoing a kill on their carry. Baiting it out with burst first, or holding damage for after the rewind, gets the kill.
spike_note: Steady early with double bombs; level 6 adds a save for his carry, and he gets more useful as items lower his cooldowns.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text

key_note: E (Sleepy Trouble Bubble) puts you to sleep after a drowsy delay and the first hit is doubled, often Q (Paddle Star!), which hurts more the longer it flies. Trading while E is on cooldown is the main window.
ult_note: R (Portal Jump) blinks her a short distance for 1 second, then blinks her back, mainly to angle Q (Paddle Star!) from further away for more damage. It is not an escape or engage, so she ends up where she started; that spot is where to catch her.
spike_note: Strong poke and burst from the early levels; level 6 makes long-range Q angles easier, and her first damage item makes one-combo kills real.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; escape 1 (W can pick up a dropped summoner spell, R returns her)

key_note: E (Grasping Roots) is her root and most of her kill pressure, and seeds near you turn into plants when she casts Q or E. Dodging E and staying away from seeds makes trades much easier; she has no dash.
ult_note: R (Stranglethorns) grows a thicket that damages enemies and knocks them airborne as it contracts, and enrages her plants inside. Grouped fights in tight spaces favor her; walking out before it contracts avoids the knock-up.
spike_note: Level 6 adds a team fight knock-up. Her damage grows with each magic damage item, and she is strongest in mid-game skirmishes around her plants.
notes: drafted from 16.19.1 ability text; early 2 or 3, chose 2
